name: ryu.honcho
description: Give the swappable `memory` layer a provider that MODELS the user instead of only storing rows, via Honcho (https://honcho.dev) — the Plastic Labs identity layer Hermes uses for exactly this. Honcho watches the messages you hand it and derives a per-peer REPRESENTATION; its Dialectic endpoint (`POST /v3/workspaces/{workspace_id}/peers/{peer_id}/chat`) then answers a natural-language question about that peer with its own synthesis. That is what the canonical `memory__context` verb has always promised and no shipped provider served, so this is the first plugin to make the kernel's `context` bridge (`memory.provider-context`) do anything at all. Honcho here serves TWO verbs: `memory__context` (the Dialectic synthesis) and `memory__search` (`POST .../peers/{peer_id}/search`, documented as "Search a Peer's messages" — conversation text, not the conclusions Honcho derives from it, which matters because the `prefetch` bridge is on by default and will start injecting message excerpts each turn). It also binds the two WRITE verbs, `memory__sync` and `memory__store`, through an adapter. Honcho's only documented write is `POST /v3/workspaces/{workspace_id}/sessions/{session_id}/messages`, whose `messages[]` items each require a `peer_id` — a NESTED position the declarative `arg_template` cannot reach, because a template substitutes only from CALLER arguments and never sees a resolved `pref:`. That is why both verbs went unbound and why `memory.mirror-builtin` (default ON) was inert. An adapter receives those `pref:` values already resolved, so the per-install peer lands inside `messages[]` without hardcoding one bucket for every install. The session and both peers are caller-named and created on first write, so nothing has to be set up by hand; Ryu's own replies are written as a SEPARATE peer, since attributing an assistant turn to your peer would poison the representation Honcho derives about you. `memory__forget` stays unbound: Honcho documents no message-delete endpoint, which no adapter can invent. The built-in store's own `memorystore__save` tool and this node's per-turn memory write are kernel and untouched. Every call is scoped to one workspace and one peer, both set per install in the settings tab — a hardcoded pair would put every install in one shared bucket. Requires a BYOK Honcho API key.
